State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Reliance Communications vs Manjit Singh on 30 May, 2012
PUNJAB STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 DAKSHIN MARG, SECTOR 37-A, CHANDIGARH

 First Appeal No.1347 of 2007

 Date of institution: 03.10.2007
 Date of decision : 30.05.2012

Reliance Communications Ltd., Zonal Office, Ranjit Avenue, SCO 3, B-
Block, Amritsar having its Circle Office at SCO 135-136, Sector 9-C,
Chandigarh through its authorized representative/signatory Shri Mast Ram
Deswal.

 .....Appellants
 Versus

Manjit Singh, 14-B, Baba Deep Singh Avenue, Near Outside Chattiwind
Gate, Amritsar.

 .....Respondent

 First Appeal against the order dated 27.08.2007
 passed by the District Consumer Disputes
 Redressal Forum, Amritsar.
Before:-
 Mr.Jagroop Singh Mahal, Presiding Judicial Member
Mr.Baldev Singh Sekhon, Member

Argued by:-
For the appellants : Sh.D.K.Singla, Advocate

 For the respondent : Sh.Manjit Singh in person

JAGROOP SINGH MAHAL, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 This is OP's appeal under
Section 15
of the Consumer

Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) against the order

dated 27.08.2007 passed by the learned District Consumer Disputes

Redressal Forum, Amritsar (in short the District Forum) vide which the OP-

appellants were directed to replace the mobile set of the complainant with a

new one of the same make and brand, failing which, to pay Rs.3905/- in cash

on return of the old mobile.
First Appeal No.1347 of 2007 2
2. The case of the complainant is that on 20.1.2006, he purchased

the mobile phone from Reliance Web World Express owned by the OP-

appellants for Rs.4200/-. It had a warranty of one year. He was given

lifetime incoming scheme but within one month of the purchase, the mobile

phone set developed defects and its battery became completely dead on

6.7.2006. The complainant lodged a report with the OP company, upon

which, he was asked to approach the Web World and when he went there,

they referred him to the OP company. He again lodged a complaint with the

OP and was asked to approach G.Tran Service Centre of the Company but

when he went at the given address, there was no such service centre.

Thereafter, he was given the address of G.Tran Service Centre of Jalandhar,

the complainant went to Jalandhar but did not find any such service station

at that place. He was then given the address of G.Tran Company at Malviya

Nagar, Delhi and when he went to Delhi, he was told to contact the Reliance

Company because their agreement with Reliance Company had expired on

31.12.2005. They refused to render service, upon which, he again contacted

the OP Company. They had been assuring to render service but did not. He

ultimately filed the present complaint on 19.12.2006.
3. A notice of the complaint was issued to the OP. They denied if

the learned District Forum at Amritsar had territorial jurisdiction to entertain

the complaint. It was alleged that reliance Infocom Limited has merged with

the Reliance Communications with effect from 12.9.2006. It was alleged that

the Consumer Forum have no jurisdiction to entertain the complaint in view

of
Section 4
and
7B
of the Indian Telegraph Act. The complaint was said to

be bad for non-joinder of M/s G. Tran Korea Inc and M/s Shree Je

Associates. The OP claimed to be a telephone service provider and not the

manufacturer of the mobile sets which are to be repaired or replaced by M/s
First Appeal No.1347 of 2007 3
G. Tran Korea Inc.. M/s Shree Je Associates was admitted to be a Reliance

Web World Express but it was an independent entity selling goods on which

they earn commission from the OP. They are said to be running the business

under franchise agreement and are not their agent. On merits, it was denied

if the mobile hand set was manufactured by them. Their contention is that

M/s G.Tran Korea is the manufacturer who used to sell the mobile hand sets

through Shree Je Associates and Reliance Infocom Limited is not liable for

any defect therein. It was admitted that the complainant had contacted them

on phone and he was guited to get the service from various places. It was

denied if the OPs are liable to repair the mobile hand set or to refund the

amount.
4. Both the parties were given opportunity to adduce evidence in

support of their contentions.
5. After hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the

parties and perusing the record, the learned District Forum allowed the

complaint in terms as mentioned above vide impugned order dated

27.8.2007. The OPs have challenged the same through this appeal.
6. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the

appellants and Manjit Singh in person respondent/complainant and have

perused the record.
7. The contention of the learned counsel for the appellants is that

the appellants are only the service provider and neither it had sold the mobile

hand set to the complainant nor was the same manufactured by them. His

contention is that the mobile hand set was manufactured by G. Tran Korea

Inc. and was sold to the complainant by Shree Je Associates, none of whom

has been made a party to the present complaint and the complaint, therefore,

cannot be allowed in the absence of the necessary parties. In support of his
First Appeal No.1347 of 2007 4
contention, he referred to the invoice Ex.C2 and the limited warranty

statement Ex.C3 issued by G Tran. The complainant, on the other hand, has

argued that no doubt the mobile hand set was purchased from Shree Je

Associates but when it developed defects, it was to be repaired by the OP.

According to him, instead of repairing the mobile hand set, they directed

him to go to the Web World, thereafter, to the Service Centre of G. Tran

Company at Mall Road, Amritsar where no such service centre was existing.

He was, then, sent to Model Town, Jalandhar to the service centre of G. Tran

but there also, no such service centre was existing. Not only this, the

complainant was then directed to go to Delhi to service centre of G. Tran in

Malviya Nagar, Delhi. They also refused to repair the handset and directed

him to contact the reliance company as their contact had already come to an

end on 31.12.2005. It shows the high handedness on the part of the OPs in

harassing their customers who had committed the mistake of purchasing

their handset. The primary responsibility of rendering service of the hand set

was, therefore, that of the OP appellants. They tried to shift it to some other

Service Centre but could not succeed. There was, therefore, clear cut

deficiency in service on their part.
8. As regards the contention of the OP-appellants that the handset

was manufactured by G. Tran who had issued Limited Warranty Ex.C3.

Again there is no truth in it. Ex.C3 does not mention the address of the said

company. The OP had also sent the complainant to 3-4 service centres of G.

Tran but those were non-existent. Ex.C2 is the sale invoice which shows that

the complainant had purchased a reliance G. Tran set. So it was basically the

handset being sold under the banner of the Reliance Company and they

cannot abdicate their responsibility to replace or repair the handset in case it

goes out of order. Even at the stage of arguments, the learned counsel for the
First Appeal No.1347 of 2007 5
appellants was unable to tell the address of G. Tran or any of its service

centres. Needless to mention that no such address was furnished to the

complainant along with Ex.C3. The subsequent information given by the OP

regarding G. Tran Service Centres was found to be wrong . It is, therefore,

not only the deficiency in service on the part of the OP-appellants but they

were harassing their customers instead of rendering proper service to them.
9. Otherwise also, there is no evidence to that effect that the

mobile hand set was manufactured by G. Tran. Simply handing over a

pamphlet in the name of a third party would not prove such a party to be

manufacturer of the hand set. When G. Tran does not appear to be existing,

the question of the complainant joining such a firm as a party did not arise. It

is true that the mobile handset was purchased by the complainant from Shree

Je Associates. Ex.C2 shows that it is Reliance Web World Express, mobile

recharge, service etc. In their written reply, the OP admitted that they were

working on commission basis. When Shree Je Associates are selling the

hand sets of the complainant, they are merely an agent of the OP and even if,

it has not been made a party, the complaint would be maintainable against

the Principal which is proved to be the manufacturer of the handset. It would

be for the OP to recover or not to recover the said amount from Shree Je

Associates.
10. In view of the above discussion, we are of the opinion that the

learned District Forum rightly allowed the complaint. There is no merit in

this appeal and the same is, accordingly, dismissed with Rs.5000/- as costs

of litigation.
11. The appellants had deposited an amount of Rs.1953/- with this

Commission at the time of filing of the appeal on 03.10.2007. This amount

of Rs.1953/- with interest accrued thereon, if any, be remitted by the registry
First Appeal No.1347 of 2007 6
to the respondent by way of a crossed cheque/demand draft after the expiry

of 45 days.
12. Copies of the orders be supplied to the parties free of costs.
(JAGROOP SINGH MAHAL)
 PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 (BALDEV SINGH SEKHON)
 MEMBER
May 30, 2012.
Paritosh
